My husband and I were raised in very different ways. I came from a patriarchal home and he came from a matriarchal one. My home was the exact opposite and I was raised with my parents constantly telling me that they were raising me to be a good wife. I think many couples have these kinds of barriers...especially after years of marriage. I received a really excellent piece of wisdom several years ago in my pursuits to strengthen/improve myself and my marriage. It was that, people tend to love one another in the way that we want to be loved, not how the other person needs/wants to be loved. That truly loving our partner means taking the time to learn how they most feel loved and meeting that need even if it feels unnatural/unusual to you. When you feel you’re showing your partner love and they aren’t regarding it as such it can build resentment, and when your partner feels they aren’t receiving the love they need the way they need the same issue arises. I still think about that wisdom when, occasionally, I feel myself balk at “all the nice things I’ve done to show him I care that he doesn’t seem to notice”. I always come back to reality and try to keep perspective on what he really needs. Maybe that will help you, maybe not. Take it with you if it does, leave it if not. :)
